headline: Pretrained protein and chemical embeddings fused with structure, dynamics and energetics for variant and site ranking
label: Learned Enzyme And Variant Prioritization
summary: New benchmarks with wet-lab validation, plus physics- and dynamics-conditioned predictors, are reshaping how enzymes, mutants and ligand sites get ranked.
synthesis: The dominant thread is ranking enzymes, mutations and binding sites using representations from pretrained protein and molecular language models, increasingly conditioned on structure, energetics or dynamics. DecoyOpt uses ESM3-generated functional-site decoys for enzyme discrimination and EC assignment; DynamicsPLM attaches residue-level and pairwise MD heads to a 35M-parameter model for zero-shot variant effects; EvoPhi-DDG averaged with JanusDDG enforces antisymmetric, thermodynamically consistent ddG; MutAtlas scores exhaustive PDB-wide single-site mutations with energy, language and inverse-folding models; HEIWA injects explicit-implicit solvent attention into ESM3 embeddings. Site-level work extends to apo/holo allosteric prediction (AllositeUltra, AsBench2), functional phosphosites, RNA small-molecule pockets, partner-specific interfaces via ProstT5 with cross-chain attention, and language-prior geometric potentials for ligand scoring. What is new is the evaluation and closed-loop turn: EnzyArena groups kinetic data by engineering campaign and finds zero-shot consensus strongest across a 150-mutant validation, NMR 15N shifts expose foundation-model error at dynamic core residues, and ProTEUS couples mutation-resolved prediction to iterative evolution.
